74:1: Interpretation of Surah Al-Muddaththir In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful It was proven in Sahih Al-Bukhari from the hadith of Yahya bin Abi Katheer on the authority of Abu Salamah on the authority of Jabir that he used to say: The first thing to be revealed from the Qur’an was O you wrapped up in garments. The majority disagreed with him and went to the view that the first thing to be revealed in the Qur’an was the saying of God Almighty: Read in the name of your Lord who created, as will come there, God willing. Al-Bukhari said: Yahya told us, Waki’ told us, on the authority of Ali ibn al-Mubarak, on the authority of Yahya ibn Abi Katheer, who said: I asked Abu Salamah ibn Abd al-Rahman about the first verse of the Qur’an to be revealed. He said: O you wrapped up in a cloak. I said: Read in the name of your Lord who created. Abu Salamah said: I asked Jabir ibn Abdullah about that and I said to him the same as you said to me. Jabir said: “I will not narrate to you except what the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) narrated to us. He said: “I stayed in Hira’ and when I had finished staying in Hira’, I dismounted and was called. I looked to my right and did not see anything, I looked to my left and did not see anything, I looked in front of me and did not see anything, and I looked behind me and did not see anything. I raised my head and saw something, so I came to Khadijah and said: ‘Cover me up and pour cold water on me.’ So they covered me up and poured cold water on me. Then the verse was revealed: ‘O you wrapped up in a cloak, arise and warn, and glorify your Lord.’” This is how he narrated it from this source. Muslim narrated it on the authority of Aqeel on the authority of Ibn Shihab on the authority of Abu Salamah who said: Jabir ibn Abdullah told me that he heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, talking about the period of revelation. He said in his hadith: “While I was walking, I heard a voice from the sky. I raised my gaze towards the sky, and behold, the angel who had come to me at Hira was sitting on a chair between the sky and the earth. I knelt down from it until I fell to the ground. I came to my family and said: Cover me, cover me, so they covered me. Then God, the Most High, revealed: ‘O you wrapped in garments! Arise and warn! And your Lord glorify! And your garments purify! And uncleanliness avoid.’ Abu Salamah said: ‘And uncleanliness is idols.’ Then the revelation became intense and continued.” This is the wording of Al-Bukhari. This is the preserved context and it indicates that the revelation had come down before this, because of his saying: ‘Then behold, the angel who had come to me at Hira’, that is Gabriel, when he came to him with his saying: ‘Read in the name of your Lord who created! Created man from a clot! Read, and your Lord is the Most Generous! Who taught by the pen! He taught.’” Man is what he does not know.” Then after this, a period occurred, and then the angel descended after this. The group pointed out that the first thing to be revealed after the period of revelation was this Surah, as Imam Ahmad said: Hajjaj told us, Laith told us, Aqil told us on the authority of Ibn Shihab, who said: I heard Abu Salamah bin Abd al-Rahman say: Jabir bin Abdullah told me that he heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: Then the revelation ceased for me for a period, and while I was walking, I heard a voice from the sky. I raised my gaze towards the sky and saw the angel who had come to me sitting on a chair between the sky and the earth, so I knelt before him in fear until I fell to the ground. I went to my family and said to them: Cover me up, cover me up, so they covered me up. Then God, the Most High, revealed: “O you wrapped in garments, arise and warn. And your Lord glorify. And your garments purify. And uncleanliness avoid.” Then the revelation became intense and continued. They both narrated it from the hadith of al-Zuhri with it. Al-Tabarani said: Muhammad bin Ali bin Shuaib Al-Sammar narrated to us, Al-Hasan bin Bishr Al-Bajali narrated to us, Al-Mu’afa bin Imran narrated to us, from Ibrahim bin Yazid: I heard Ibn Abi Malekah say: I heard Ibn Abbas say: Al-Walid bin Al-Mughirah made food for the Quraysh, and when they ate from it, he said: What do you say about this man? Some of them said: He is a magician, and some of them said: He is not a magician, and some of them said: He is a soothsayer, and some of them said: He is not a soothsayer, and some of them said: He is a poet, and some of them said: He is not a poet, and some of them said: Rather, it is an effective magic. They agreed that it is an effective magic. report of that reached the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him), so he became sad, covered his head and wrapped himself up, so God revealed: O you wrapped up in garments! Arise and warn! And your Lord glorify! And your garments purify! And uncleanliness shun! And do not confer favor, expecting more! And for your Lord be patient. And His statement: Arise and warn means roll up the sleeves of resolve and warn the people. And with this, the sending was accomplished, just as the first time, the prophecy was accomplished. "And your Lord, so glorify" means magnify. And the Almighty's saying: "And your garments purify Al-Ajlah Al-Kindi said on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas that a man came to him and asked him about this verse And your garments purify" He said: Do not wear them for disobedience or for treachery. Then he said: Haven't you heard the saying of Ghailan bin Salamah Al-Thaqafi: By the grace of God, I do not wear the garment of an immoral person, nor do I cover myself with treachery. Ibn Jurayj said on the authority of Ata’ on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding the verse And your garments purify He said: In the speech of the Arabs, clean clothes. In a narration with this chain of transmission, it means purify from sins. Ibrahim, Ash-Sha’bi and Ata’ said the same. Ath-Thawri said on the authority of a man on the authority of Ata’ on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding this verse And your garments purify He said: From sin. Ibrahim An-Nakha’i said the same. Mujahid said: And your garments purify He said: Your soul, not your clothes. In a narration on his authority: And your garments purify meaning your deeds, so put them right. Abu Razin said the same. He said in another narration: And your garments purify meaning you are not a soothsayer or a magician, so ignore what they said. Qatadah said: And your garments purify meaning purify them from sins. The Arabs used to call a man who broke his covenant with God dirty clothes, and if he fulfilled his promise and put them right, he said pure clothes. Ikrimah and Ad-Dahhak said: Do not wear it while committing a sin. The poet said: If a person does not defile his honor with meanness, then every garment he wears is beautiful. Al-Awfi said on the authority of Ibn Abbas, And your garments purify meaning do not let the garments you wear come from impure earnings. It is also said, Do not wear your garments in disobedience. Muhammad ibn Sirin said, And your garments purify meaning wash them with water. Ibn Zayd said, The polytheists did not purify themselves, so God commanded him to purify himself and to purify his garments. This statement was chosen by Ibn Jarir. The verse may include all of that along with purity of the heart, as the Arabs use the word clothes to refer to it, as Imru’ al-Qais said: Fatima, take it easy, stop being so spoiled. If you have decided to leave me, then be patient. If you are displeased with my behavior, then ask for my clothes from your clothes and you will be free Saeed bin Jubair said: And your clothing purify and your heart and intention purify. Muhammad bin Kaab Al-Qurazi and Al-Hasan Al-Basri said: And your character improve. And the Almighty’s statement: And avoid uncleanliness Ali bin Abi Talha said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: And uncleanliness is idols, so avoid. And this is what Mujahid, Ikrimah, Qatadah, Al-Zuhri and Ibn Zayd said: They are the idols. Ibrahim and Al-Dahhak said: And avoid uncleanliness means leave sin. In any case, it is not necessary to be involved in any of that, like the Almighty’s statement: O Prophet, fear God and do not obey the disbelievers and the hypocrites and And Moses said to his brother Aaron, “Take my place among my people and do good and do not follow the way of the corrupters. God the Almighty said: {And do not bestow a favor, expecting to receive more in return.} Ibn Abbas said: Do not give a gift seeking more in return. This is what Ikrimah, Mujahid, Ata’, Tawus, Abu Al-Ahwas, Ibrahim Al-Nakha’i, Ad-Dahhak, Qatadah, As-Suddi and others said. It was narrated on the authority of Ibn Mas’ud that he recited: {And do not bestow a favor, expecting to receive more in return.} Al-Hasan Al-Basri said: Do not bestow a favor upon your Lord by doing good deeds, expecting to receive more in return. This is what Ar-Rabi’ ibn Anas said, and Ibn Jarir preferred this view. Khasif said on the authority of Mujahid, regarding God the Almighty’s saying: {And do not bestow a favor, expecting to receive more in return.} He said: To bestow a favor in Arabic means to become weak. Ibn Zayd said: Do not bestow prophethood upon people, expecting them to gain it, and take worldly compensation for it. So there are four opinions, and the first is the most correct, and God knows best. God the Almighty says: {And for the sake of your Lord be patient} meaning, make your patience in the face of their harm for the sake of your Lord, the Almighty and Majestic. This was said by Mujahid. Ibrahim Al-Nakha’i said: Be patient, your gift is from God the Almighty. God the Almighty says: {Then when the Trumpet is blown, that will be a difficult Day, for the disbelievers - not easy} Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, Al-Sha’bi, Zaid bin Aslam, Al-Hasan, Qatadah, Al-Dahhak, Al-Rabi bin Anas, Al-Suddi and Ibn Zaid said: The Trumpet means the trumpet. Mujahid said: It is in the shape of a horn. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Saeed Al-Ashj narrated to us, Asbat bin Muhammad narrated to us, on the authority of Mutraf, on the authority of Atiyyah Al-Awfi, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, When the trumpet is blown, and he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: How can I be at ease while the companion of the horn has taken hold of the trumpet and bent his forehead, waiting for the command to blow it? He said: The companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: What do you command us, O Messenger of God? He said: “Say: God is sufficient for us, and He is the best Disposer of affairs. In God we trust.” And this is how Imam Ahmad narrated it on the authority of Asbat, on his authority. Ibn Jarir narrated it on the authority of Abu Kurayb, on the authority of Ibn Fadil, and Asbat, both of them on the authority of Mutraf, on his authority. And he narrated it through another chain of transmission on the authority of Al-Awfi, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, on his authority. And the Almighty’s saying: Then that Day will be a difficult Day means severe for the disbelievers, not easy meaning not easy for them, as the Almighty said: The disbelievers will say, ‘This is a difficult Day’. We have narrated on the authority of Zurarah ibn Awfa, the judge of Basra, that he led them in the dawn prayer, and he recited this surah. When he reached the Almighty’s saying: Then when the trumpet is blown, * That will be a difficult Day * For the disbelievers, not easy, he gasped and then fell down dead. May God Almighty have mercy on him.

Al-Bukhari said: Yahya told us, Waki’ told us, on the authority of Ali ibn al-Mubarak, on the authority of Yahya ibn Abi Katheer, who said: I asked Abu Salamah ibn Abd al-Rahman about the first verse of the Qur’an to be revealed. He said: O you wrapped up in a cloak. I said: Read in the name of your Lord who created. Abu Salamah said: I asked Jabir ibn Abdullah about that and I said to him the same as you said to me. Jabir said: “I will not narrate to you except what the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) narrated to us. He said: “I stayed in Hira’ and when I had finished staying in Hira’, I dismounted and was called. I looked to my right and did not see anything, I looked to my left and did not see anything, I looked in front of me and did not see anything, and I looked behind me and did not see anything. I raised my head and saw something, so I came to Khadijah and said: ‘Cover me up and pour cold water on me.’ So they covered me up and poured cold water on me. Then the verse was revealed: ‘O you wrapped up in a cloak, arise and warn, and glorify your Lord.’” This is how he narrated it from this source. Muslim narrated it on the authority of Aqeel on the authority of Ibn Shihab on the authority of Abu Salamah who said: Jabir ibn Abdullah told me that he heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, talking about the period of revelation. He said in his hadith: “While I was walking, I heard a voice from the sky. I raised my gaze towards the sky, and behold, the angel who had come to me at Hira was sitting on a chair between the sky and the earth. I knelt down from it until I fell to the ground. I came to my family and said: Cover me, cover me, so they covered me. Then God, the Most High, revealed: ‘O you wrapped in garments! Arise and warn! And your Lord glorify! And your garments purify! And uncleanliness avoid.’ Abu Salamah said: ‘And uncleanliness is idols.’ Then the revelation became intense and continued.” This is the wording of Al-Bukhari. This is the preserved context and it indicates that the revelation had come down before this, because of his saying: ‘Then behold, the angel who had come to me at Hira’, that is Gabriel, when he came to him with his saying: ‘Read in the name of your Lord who created! Created man from a clot! Read, and your Lord is the Most Generous! Who taught by the pen! He taught.’” Man is what he does not know.” Then after this, a period occurred, and then the angel descended after this. The group pointed out that the first thing to be revealed after the period of revelation was this Surah, as Imam Ahmad said: Hajjaj told us, Laith told us, Aqil told us on the authority of Ibn Shihab, who said: I heard Abu Salamah bin Abd al-Rahman say: Jabir bin Abdullah told me that he heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: Then the revelation ceased for me for a period, and while I was walking, I heard a voice from the sky. I raised my gaze towards the sky and saw the angel who had come to me sitting on a chair between the sky and the earth, so I knelt before him in fear until I fell to the ground. I went to my family and said to them: Cover me up, cover me up, so they covered me up. Then God, the Most High, revealed: “O you wrapped in garments, arise and warn. And your Lord glorify. And your garments purify. And uncleanliness avoid.” Then the revelation became intense and continued. They both narrated it from the hadith of al-Zuhri with it. Al-Tabarani said: Muhammad bin Ali bin Shuaib Al-Sammar narrated to us, Al-Hasan bin Bishr Al-Bajali narrated to us, Al-Mu’afa bin Imran narrated to us, from Ibrahim bin Yazid: I heard Ibn Abi Malekah say: I heard Ibn Abbas say: Al-Walid bin Al-Mughirah made food for the Quraysh, and when they ate from it, he said: What do you say about this man? Some of them said: He is a magician, and some of them said: He is not a magician, and some of them said: He is a soothsayer, and some of them said: He is not a soothsayer, and some of them said: He is a poet, and some of them said: He is not a poet, and some of them said: Rather, it is an effective magic. They agreed that it is an effective magic. report of that reached the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him), so he became sad, covered his head and wrapped himself up, so God revealed: O you wrapped up in garments! Arise and warn! And your Lord glorify! And your garments purify! And uncleanliness shun! And do not confer favor, expecting more! And for your Lord be patient. And His statement: Arise and warn means roll up the sleeves of resolve and warn the people. And with this, the sending was accomplished, just as the first time, the prophecy was accomplished. And your Lord, so glorify means magnify. And the Almighty's saying: And your garments purify Al-Ajlah Al-Kindi said on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas that a man came to him and asked him about this verse And your garments purify He said: Do not wear them for disobedience or for treachery. Then he said: Haven't you heard the saying of Ghailan bin Salamah Al-Thaqafi: By the grace of God, I do not wear the garment of an immoral person, nor do I cover myself with treachery. Ibn Jurayj said on the authority of Ata’ on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding the verse And your garments purify He said: In the speech of the Arabs, clean clothes. In a narration with this chain of transmission, it means purify from sins. Ibrahim, Ash-Sha’bi and Ata’ said the same. Ath-Thawri said on the authority of a man on the authority of Ata’ on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding this verse And your garments purify He said: From sin. Ibrahim An-Nakha’i said the same. Mujahid said: And your garments purify He said: Your soul, not your clothes. In a narration on his authority: And your garments purify meaning your deeds, so put them right. Abu Razin said the same. He said in another narration: And your garments purify meaning you are not a soothsayer or a magician, so ignore what they said. Qatadah said: And your garments purify meaning purify them from sins. The Arabs used to call a man who broke his covenant with God dirty clothes, and if he fulfilled his promise and put them right, he said pure clothes. Ikrimah and Ad-Dahhak said: Do not wear it while committing a sin. The poet said: If a person does not defile his honor with meanness, then every garment he wears is beautiful. Al-Awfi said on the authority of Ibn Abbas, And your garments purify meaning do not let the garments you wear come from impure earnings. It is also said, Do not wear your garments in disobedience. Muhammad ibn Sirin said, And your garments purify meaning wash them with water. Ibn Zayd said, The polytheists did not purify themselves, so God commanded him to purify himself and to purify his garments. This statement was chosen by Ibn Jarir. The verse may include all of that along with purity of the heart, as the Arabs use the word clothes to refer to it, as Imru’ al-Qais said: Fatima, take it easy, stop being so spoiled. If you have decided to leave me, then be patient. If you are displeased with my behavior, then ask for my clothes from your clothes and you will be free Saeed bin Jubair said: And your clothing purify and your heart and intention purify. Muhammad bin Kaab Al-Qurazi and Al-Hasan Al-Basri said: And your character improve. And the Almighty’s statement: And avoid uncleanliness Ali bin Abi Talha said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: And uncleanliness is idols, so avoid. And this is what Mujahid, Ikrimah, Qatadah, Al-Zuhri and Ibn Zayd said: They are the idols. Ibrahim and Al-Dahhak said: And avoid uncleanliness means leave sin. In any case, it is not necessary to be involved in any of that, like the Almighty’s statement: O Prophet, fear God and do not obey the disbelievers and the hypocrites and And Moses said to his brother Aaron, “Take my place among my people and do good and do not follow the way of the corrupters. God the Almighty said: {And do not bestow a favor, expecting to receive more in return.} Ibn Abbas said: Do not give a gift seeking more in return. This is what Ikrimah, Mujahid, Ata’, Tawus, Abu Al-Ahwas, Ibrahim Al-Nakha’i, Ad-Dahhak, Qatadah, As-Suddi and others said. It was narrated on the authority of Ibn Mas’ud that he recited: {And do not bestow a favor, expecting to receive more in return.} Al-Hasan Al-Basri said: Do not bestow a favor upon your Lord by doing good deeds, expecting to receive more in return. This is what Ar-Rabi’ ibn Anas said, and Ibn Jarir preferred this view. Khasif said on the authority of Mujahid, regarding God the Almighty’s saying: {And do not bestow a favor, expecting to receive more in return.} He said: To bestow a favor in Arabic means to become weak. Ibn Zayd said: Do not bestow prophethood upon people, expecting them to gain it, and take worldly compensation for it. So there are four opinions, and the first is the most correct, and God knows best. God the Almighty says: {And for the sake of your Lord be patient} meaning, make your patience in the face of their harm for the sake of your Lord, the Almighty and Majestic. This was said by Mujahid. Ibrahim Al-Nakha’i said: Be patient, your gift is from God the Almighty. God the Almighty says: {Then when the Trumpet is blown, that will be a difficult Day, for the disbelievers - not easy} Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, Al-Sha’bi, Zaid bin Aslam, Al-Hasan, Qatadah, Al-Dahhak, Al-Rabi bin Anas, Al-Suddi and Ibn Zaid said: The Trumpet means the trumpet. Mujahid said: It is in the shape of a horn. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Saeed Al-Ashj narrated to us, Asbat bin Muhammad narrated to us, on the authority of Mutraf, on the authority of Atiyyah Al-Awfi, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, When the trumpet is blown, and he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: How can I be at ease while the companion of the horn has taken hold of the trumpet and bent his forehead, waiting for the command to blow it? He said: The companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: What do you command us, O Messenger of God? He said: “Say: God is sufficient for us, and He is the best Disposer of affairs. In God we trust.” And this is how Imam Ahmad narrated it on the authority of Asbat, on his authority. Ibn Jarir narrated it on the authority of Abu Kurayb, on the authority of Ibn Fadil, and Asbat, both of them on the authority of Mutraf, on his authority. And he narrated it through another chain of transmission on the authority of Al-Awfi, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, on his authority. And the Almighty’s saying: Then that Day will be a difficult Day means severe for the disbelievers, not easy meaning not easy for them, as the Almighty said: The disbelievers will say, ‘This is a difficult Day’. We have narrated on the authority of Zurarah ibn Awfa, the judge of Basra, that he led them in the dawn prayer, and he recited this surah. When he reached the Almighty’s saying: Then when the trumpet is blown, * That will be a difficult Day * For the disbelievers, not easy, he gasped and then fell down dead. May God Almighty have mercy on him.

Then he said: It is strange and we do not know it except from the hadith of Ibn Lahi’ah, on the authority of Diraj, and this is what he said. Ibn Jarir narrated it on the authority of Yunus, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Wahb, on the authority of Amr ibn al-Harith, on the authority of Diraj, and it contains strangeness and oddity. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Zur’ah and Ali ibn Abd al-Rahman, known as ‘Allan al-Muqri, told us: Munajab told us, Sharik told us, on the authority of ‘Ammar al-Dahni, on the authority of ‘Atiyyah al-‘Awfi, on the authority of Abu Sa’id, on the authority of the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, I will make him ascend with difficulty. He said: “It is a mountain of fire in Hell which he is commanded to climb. When he places his hand down, it melts and when he raises it, it returns. When he places his foot down, it melts and when he raises it, it returns.” Al-Bazzar and Ibn Jarir narrated it from the hadith of Sharik with this chain of transmission. Qatada said, on the authority of Ibn ‘Abbas: Ascending is a rock in Hell upon which the disbeliever is dragged on his face. Al-Suddi said: Ascending is a smooth rock in Hell which he is commanded to climb. Mujahid said: I will make him ascend with difficulty means with difficulty from the torment. Qatada said: A torment in which there is no rest, and Ibn Jarir preferred this. And the Almighty’s saying: He thought and measured means that We made him suffer a severe ascent, meaning that We brought him close to the arduous torment due to his distance from faith, because he thought and measured, meaning he pondered what he would say in the Qur’an when he was asked about the Qur’an, so he thought, what would he fabricate from the statement. And measured means he pondered. “So he killed, how he measured. Then he killed, how he measured.” A supplication against him. Then he looked means he looked again and pondered. Then he frowned means he closed his eyes and frowned. And he frowned means he was grim and hated. From this is the saying of Tawbah ibn al-Humayr: I was disturbed by her aversion and her turning away from my needs and her stubbornness. And his saying: Then he turned away and was arrogant means he turned away from the truth and returned in a haughty retreat, arrogant about submitting to the Qur’an. Then he said, ‘This is nothing but magic that is being transmitted’ meaning this is magic that Muhammad transmits from others who came before him and relates it from them. For this reason he said, This is nothing but the word of a human being, meaning it is not the word of God. The one mentioned in this context is Al-Walid ibn Al-Mughirah Al-Makhzumi, one of the leaders of Quraysh, may God curse him. Among his stories in this is what Al-Awfi narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: Al-Walid ibn Al-Mughirah entered upon Abu Bakr ibn Abi Quhafah and asked him about the Qur’an. When he told him, he went out to Quraysh and said, “How strange is what Ibn Abi Kabshah is saying. By God, it is neither poetry nor magic nor madness, and his words are the words of God.” When the group of Quraysh heard that, they gathered and said, By God, if Al-Walid converts to Islam, Quraysh will convert to Islam. When Abu Jahl ibn Hisham heard that, he said, By God, I will suffice you in his matter. So he went until he entered his house and said to Al-Walid, Did you not see that your people have gathered against you? Alms? He said: Are you not the one with the most wealth and children? Abu Jahl said: They say that you only go to Ibn Abi Quhafah to get some of his food. Al-Walid said: Do my clan talk about it? No, by God, I will not come near Ibn Abi Quhafah, nor Umar, nor Ibn Abi Kabshah. His words are nothing but magic that has been passed on. Then God revealed to His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace: Leave Me and he whom I created alone until His saying: Leave nothing behind and spare nothing. Qatada said: They claimed that he said: By God, I looked at what the man said and saw that it was not poetry, but rather it had a sweetness to it, and it had a freshness to it, and it was rising above and above what was rising above it. I have no doubt that it was magic. Then God revealed: So kill, how was it decreed? The verse. Then he frowned and frowned. He closed his eyes and frowned. Ibn Jarir said: Ibn Abd al-A'la told us, Muhammad ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Ibad ibn Mansur, on the authority of Ikrimah, that al-Walid ibn al-Mughira came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and recited the Qur'an to him, and it seemed that he felt sorry for him. report of that reached Abu Jahl ibn Hisham, so he came to him and said, "O uncle, your people want to collect money for you. He said, Why?" He said: They will give it to you, for you came to Muhammad, exposing what came before him. He said: The Quraysh know that I am the richest of them. He said: Then say a word about him that will make your people know that you deny what he said and that you hate it. He said: Then what should I say about him? By God, there is no man among you who is more knowledgeable about poetry than me, nor do I know its rajaz, its qasida, nor the poetry of the jinn. By God, the one who says does not resemble anything of this. By God, the words he says have sweetness, and they crush what is beneath them, and they rise above what is raised. He said: By God, your people will not be satisfied until you say something about him. He said: Then leave me until I think about him. When he thought about him, he said: This is nothing but magic that he prefers over others. Then the verse was revealed: Leave me and he whom I created alone until he reached nineteen. Muhammad ibn Ishaq and others mentioned something similar to this. Al-Suddi claimed that when they gathered in Dar al-Nadwa to agree on a statement to say about him before the Arab delegations came to them for Hajj to turn them away from it, some said: A poet, others said: A magician, and others said: A soothsayer. Others: Crazy as God the Almighty said: See how they have put forth for you examples, but have gone astray and are unable to find a way. All this while Al-Walid was thinking about what to say about him, so he thought, estimated, looked, frowned and became sad, then he said: This is nothing but magic that is being transmitted. This is nothing but the words of humans. God the Almighty said: I will cast him into Hellfire, meaning I will immerse him in it from all sides. Then God the Almighty said: And what will make you know what Hellfire is? This is an exaggeration and glorification of its matter. Then He explained that with His Almighty saying: It leaves nothing and spares nothing, meaning it consumes their flesh, veins, nerves and skin, then replaces them with something else, and in that they neither die nor live. This was said by Ibn Buraidah, Abu Sinan and others. God the Almighty said: "A scorch for mankind." Mujahid said: meaning for the skin. Abu Razin said: It scorches the skin with a scorch, leaving it black as night. Zayd ibn Aslam said: Their bodies scorch upon it. Qatada said: "A scorch for mankind" meaning a burning of the skin. Ibn Abbas said: It burns the human complexion. God the Almighty said: "Over it are nineteen" meaning from the foremost of the guards of Hell, of great creation and rough disposition. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Zur’ah told us, Ibrahim bin Musa told us, Ibn Abi Zaydah told us, Harith told me, on the authority of Aamir, on the authority of Al-Bara’, regarding the words of God Almighty: Over it are nineteen. He said: A group of Jews asked a man from the companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, about the keepers of Hell. He said: God and His Messenger know best. The man came and informed the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and God Almighty revealed to him at that time: Over it are nineteen. He informed his companions and said: “Call them. I will ask them about the soil of Paradise if they come to me. It is white dirt.” So they came to him and asked him about the keepers of Hell. He raised his fingers twice and held his thumb back the second time, then he said: Tell me about the soil of Paradise. They said: Tell them, O Ibn Salam. He said: It is like white bread. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Bread is only made of dirt. This is how it was narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim on the authority of Al-Bara’, and it is well-known on the authority of Jabir bin Abdullah, as Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr Al-Bazzar said in His Musnad: Mandah narrated to us, Ahmad ibn Abdah narrated to us, Sufyan and Yahya ibn Hakim informed us, Sufyan narrated to us, on the authority of Mujalid, on the authority of al-Sha’bi, on the authority of Jabir ibn Abdullah, may God be pleased with him, who said: “A man came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: ‘O Muhammad, your companions have been defeated today.’ He said: ‘In what way?’ He said: ‘The Jews asked them: Did your Prophet inform you of the number of the keepers of the people of Hell?’ They said: ‘We do not know until we ask our Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace.’ The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘Are people defeated when they ask about what they do not know?’ They said: ‘We do not know until we ask our Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace.’ Bring me the enemies of God, but they had already asked their Prophet to show them God openly. So he sent for them and called them. They said: ‘O Abu al-Qasim, how many are the keepers of the people of Hell?’ He said: ‘Like this.’ Then he clasped his hands together, then he clasped them together twice and folded one over the other. He said to his companions: ‘If you are asked about the soil of Paradise, it is the dirham.’ When they asked him and he informed them about the number of the keepers of the people of Hell, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to them: ‘What is the soil of Paradise?’ So some of them looked at each other and said: “A loaf of bread, O Abu al-Qasim.” He said: Bread is made from dirhams. And this is how al-Tirmidhi narrated it at this verse on the authority of Ibn Abi Umar on the authority of Sufyan on his authority. He and al-Bazzar said that it is not known except from the hadith of Mujalid. Imam Ahmad narrated it on the authority of Ali ibn al-Madini on the authority of Sufyan, but he only related the dirhams.
74:31: God Almighty says: And We have not made the keepers of the Fire except angels that is, its guardians except angels stern and strong guardians. This was a response to the polytheists of Quraysh when they mentioned the number of guardians and Abu Jahl said: O people of Quraysh, can’t every ten of you take on one of them so that you can overcome them? God Almighty said: And We have not made the keepers of the Fire except angels that is, of strong character who cannot be resisted or overcome. It was said that Abu al-Ashdayn, whose name was Kalda ibn Asid ibn Khalaf, said: O people of Quraysh, spare me from two of them and I will spare you from seventeen of them, out of his admiration for himself. He had reached such strength, as they claim, that he would stand on a cowhide and ten people would wrestle with it to pull it out from under his feet, but the skin would tear and he would not budge. Al-Suhayli said: He is the one who invited the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, to wrestle with him, and he said: If you defeat me, I will believe in you. So the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, defeated him repeatedly, but he did not believe. Ibn Ishaq attributed the story of the wrestling to Rukanah ibn Abd Yazid ibn Hashim ibn al-Muttalib. I said: There is no contradiction between what they mentioned, and God knows best. God the Almighty says: {And We have not made their number except as a trial for those who disbelieve} meaning, We only mentioned their number, that they were nineteen, as a test from Us for the people, {that those who were given the Scripture may be certain} meaning, that they may know that this Messenger is the truth, for he spoke in accordance with what they have of the heavenly books revealed to the prophets before him, {and those who believe may increase in faith} meaning, to their faith, meaning to what they witness of the truthfulness of the report of their Prophet Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him, {and that those who were given the Scripture and the believers may not doubt, and that those in whose hearts is hypocrisy and the disbelievers may say, What does God intend by this as an example?} meaning, they say, What is the wisdom in mentioning this here? God the Almighty says: {Thus does God leave astray whom He wills and guides whom He wills} meaning, from the likes of this and similar things, faith is confirmed in the hearts of some people and shakes in others, and that is the ultimate wisdom and conclusive proof. And the Almighty’s saying: And none knows the soldiers of your Lord except Him means none knows their number and their great number except Him, lest anyone should imagine that they are only nineteen, as was said by a group of the people of misguidance and ignorance, and by the Greek philosophers and those who followed them from the two religions who heard this verse and wanted to apply it to the ten minds and nine souls whose claim they invented and were unable to establish the evidence for its requirements, so they understood the beginning of this verse and disbelieved in its end, which is His saying: And none knows the soldiers of your Lord except Him. And it was proven in the hadith of the Night Journey narrated in the two Sahihs and others on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said in describing the Frequented House in the seventh heaven: And behold, seventy thousand angels enter it every day and they do not return to it until the last thing they are responsible for. Imam Ahmad said: Aswad told us, Isra’il told us, on the authority of Ibrahim bin Muhajir, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Mawariq, on the authority of Abu Dharr, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “I see what you do not see and I hear what you do not hear. The heavens groan, and it is right for them to groan. There is not in it the space of a finger but upon it is an angel prostrating. If you knew what I know, you would laugh little and cry much, and you would not take pleasure in women on the beds, and you would go out to the high places, beseeching God Almighty.” Abu Dharr said: By God, I would like to be a tree that is being cut down. Al-Tirmidhi and Ibn Majah narrated it from the hadith of Isra’il. Al-Tirmidhi said: It is a good, rare hadith, and it is narrated on the authority of Abu Dharr as a continuation of the hadith. Al-Hafiz Abu al-Qasim al-Tabarani said: Khair bin Arfa al-Misri told us, Urwah bin Marwan al-Raqi told us, Ubayd God bin Amr told us, on the authority of Abdul Karim bin Malik, on the authority of Ata’ bin Abi Rabah, on the authority of Jabir bin Abdullah, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: There is not in the seven heavens the space of a foot, a handspan, or a palm but that there is an angel in it. A standing angel, a prostrating angel, or a kneeling angel. Then, on the Day of Resurrection, they will all say, Glory be to You! We have not worshipped You as You should be worshipped except that we have not associated anything with You. Muhammad ibn Nasr al-Marwazi said in the Book of Prayer: Amr ibn Zararah told us, Abd al-Wahhab ibn Ata’ told us, on the authority of Sa’id, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Safwan ibn Mahraz, on the authority of Hakim ibn Hizam, who said: While the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) was with his companions, he said to them, Do you hear what I hear? They said, We do not hear anything. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said, “I hear the creaking of the sky, and you are not to be blamed for it creaking. There is not a place the size of a handspan in it except that there is an angel kneeling or prostrating on it.” He also said: Muhammad bin Abdullah bin Qahdhadh narrated to us, Abu Muadh al-Fadl bin Khalid al-Nahwi narrated to us, Ubayd bin Sulayman al-Bahili narrated to us, I heard al-Dahhak bin Muzahim narrating on the authority of Masruq bin al-Ajda’ on the authority of Aisha that she said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “There is not a place of a foot in the lowest heaven except that there is an angel prostrating or standing on it. This is the saying of the angels: ‘And there is not one of Us but has a known position. And indeed, it is We who arrange [our ranks] in rows. And indeed, it is We who glorify [God].” This is a very strange chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet. Then he narrated it on the authority of Mahmud bin Adam on the authority of Abu Mu’awiyah on the authority of al-A’mash on the authority of Abu al-Dahha on the authority of Masruq on the authority of Ibn Mas’ud that he said: There is a heaven in which there is not a place the size of a handspan except that there is an angel’s forehead or feet standing on it. Then he recited: ‘And indeed, it is We who arrange [our ranks] in rows. And indeed, it is We who glorify [God].’” Then he said: Ahmad bin Sayyar told us, Abu Ja`far bin Muhammad bin Khalid al-Dimashqi, known as Ibn Ummah, told us, al-Mughira bin `Umar bin `Atiyya from Banu `Amr bin `Awf told us, Sulayman bin Ayyub told me on the authority of Salim bin `Awf, `Ata` bin Zayd bin Mas`ud from Banu al-Hubla told me, Sulayman bin `Amr bin al-Rabi` from Banu Salim told me, `Abd al-Rahman bin al-`Ala` from Banu Sa`idah told me on the authority of his father al-`Ala` bin Sa`d, who witnessed the conquest and what came after it, that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said one day to those sitting with him: Do you hear what I hear? They said: And what do you hear, O Messenger of God? He said: “The heavens groaned, and it is right for them to groan, for there is not a place for a foot in it but that there is an angel standing, bowing, or prostrating on it. And the angels said: ‘And indeed, it is We who arrange [our ranks] and indeed, it is We who glorify.’” This is a very strange chain of transmission. Then he said: Ishaq bin Muhammad bin Ismail Al-Farawi told us, Abdul Malik bin Qudamah told us, on the authority of Abdul Rahman bin Abdullah bin Dinar, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abdullah bin Omar, “That Omar came while the prayer was being performed and three men were sitting, one of them being Abu Jahsh Al-Laithi. He said: Stand up and pray with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. Two of them stood up, but Abu Jahsh refused to stand up and said: I will not stand up until a man comes who is two arms stronger than me and has more power than me, and he wrestles me down and then thrusts my face into the dirt. Omar said: So I wrestled him down and thrust his face into the dirt. Then Uthman bin Affan came and held me back from him. Omar went out angrily until he reached the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: What do you think, O Abu Hafs? He mentioned to him what had happened, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: If Omar is pleased with him, by God, I would have liked you to bring me the head of the wicked man. Omar stood up and headed towards him, and when he was far away, he called him and said: Sit down so that I may tell you how the Lord, Blessed and Exalted be He, did not care about the prayer of Abu Jahsh, and that God, the Most High, has angels in the lowest heaven who are humble and do not raise their heads.” Their heads will be raised until the Hour comes. When it comes, they will raise their heads and say, Our Lord, we did not worship You as You should be worshipped. Indeed, in the second heaven there are angels prostrating themselves and they will not raise their heads until the Hour comes. When the Hour comes, they will raise their heads and say, Glory be to You, our Lord, we did not worship You as You should be worshipped. Umar said to him: And what do they say, O Messenger of God? He said: “As for the people of the lowest heaven, they say: ‘Glory be to the Possessor of dominion and sovereignty.’ As for the people of the second heaven, they say: ‘Glory be to the Possessor of glory and majesty.’ As for the people of the third heaven, they say: ‘Glory be to the Ever-Living who does not die.’ So say it, O Umar, in your prayer.” Umar said: O Messenger of God, what about what you taught me and commanded me to say in my prayer? He said: Say this once and this once. What he commanded him to say was: I seek refuge in your pardon from your punishment, and I seek refuge in your pleasure from your wrath, and I seek refuge in you from you, the Majestic is your face. This is a very strange hadith, in fact it is extremely strange. Al-Bukhari narrated from Ishaq al-Farawi, and Ibn Hibban mentioned him among the trustworthy ones, but Abu Dawud, al-Nasa’i, al-Uqayli, and al-Darqutni declared him weak. Abu Hatim al-Razi said: He was truthful, except that he lost his sight, so he was probably prompted, and his books are authentic. He said once: He is confused. His sheikh, Abd al-Malik ibn Qudamah, Abu Qatada al-Jumahi, also spoke against him. It is surprising that Imam Muhammad bin Nasr narrated it without speaking about it, nor knowing its condition, nor discussing the weakness of some of its men. However, he narrated it from another chain of transmission on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, with a similar mursal, and from another chain of transmission on the authority of Al-Hasan Al-Basri, with a similar mursal, close to it. Then Muhammad bin Nasr said: Muhammad bin Abdullah bin Quhadadh told us, Al-Nadr told us, Ibad bin Mansur told us: I heard Adi bin Artah, while he was delivering a sermon to us on the pulpit of Al-Madain, saying: I heard a man from the companions of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: “God Almighty has angels whose limbs tremble with fear of Him. There is not an angel among them who sheds a tear except that it falls on an angel praying. Among them are angels who have been prostrating since God created the heavens and the earth, and they have not raised their heads and will not raise them until the Day of Resurrection. Among them are angels who are bowing, and they have not raised their heads since God created the heavens and the earth and will not raise them until the Day of Resurrection. When they raise their heads, they look at the face of God, the Almighty and Majestic, and say: Glory be to You, we have not worshipped You as You should be worshipped.” This is a good chain of transmission. And the Almighty said: And it is not but a reminder to mankind. Mujahid and others said: And it is not meaning the fire that was described but a reminder to mankind. Then the Almighty said: No! By the moon * And the night when it departs meaning it turns away And the morning when it brightens meaning it shines Indeed, it is one of the greatest meaning the greatest things, meaning the fire. This was said by Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, Qatadah, Ad-Dahhak and others from the Salaf. A warner to mankind * For whoever among you wills to come forward or stay behind meaning for whoever wills to accept the warning and be guided to the truth or stay behind from it and turn away and reject it.

This was a response to the polytheists of Quraysh when they mentioned the number of guardians and Abu Jahl said: O people of Quraysh, can’t every ten of you take on one of them so that you can overcome them? God Almighty said: And We have not made the keepers of the Fire except angels that is, of strong character who cannot be resisted or overcome. It was said that Abu al-Ashdayn, whose name was Kalda ibn Asid ibn Khalaf, said: O people of Quraysh, spare me from two of them and I will spare you from seventeen of them, out of his admiration for himself. He had reached such strength, as they claim, that he would stand on a cowhide and ten people would wrestle with it to pull it out from under his feet, but the skin would tear and he would not budge. Al-Suhayli said: He is the one who invited the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, to wrestle with him, and he said: If you defeat me, I will believe in you. So the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, defeated him repeatedly, but he did not believe. Ibn Ishaq attributed the story of the wrestling to Rukanah ibn Abd Yazid ibn Hashim ibn al-Muttalib. I said: There is no contradiction between what they mentioned, and God knows best. God the Almighty says: {And We have not made their number except as a trial for those who disbelieve} meaning, We only mentioned their number, that they were nineteen, as a test from Us for the people, {that those who were given the Scripture may be certain} meaning, that they may know that this Messenger is the truth, for he spoke in accordance with what they have of the heavenly books revealed to the prophets before him, {and those who believe may increase in faith} meaning, to their faith, meaning to what they witness of the truthfulness of the report of their Prophet Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him, {and that those who were given the Scripture and the believers may not doubt, and that those in whose hearts is hypocrisy and the disbelievers may say, What does God intend by this as an example?} meaning, they say, What is the wisdom in mentioning this here? God the Almighty says: {Thus does God leave astray whom He wills and guides whom He wills} meaning, from the likes of this and similar things, faith is confirmed in the hearts of some people and shakes in others, and that is the ultimate wisdom and conclusive proof. And the Almighty’s saying: And none knows the soldiers of your Lord except Him means none knows their number and their great number except Him, lest anyone should imagine that they are only nineteen, as was said by a group of the people of misguidance and ignorance, and by the Greek philosophers and those who followed them from the two religions who heard this verse and wanted to apply it to the ten minds and nine souls whose claim they invented and were unable to establish the evidence for its requirements, so they understood the beginning of this verse and disbelieved in its end, which is His saying: And none knows the soldiers of your Lord except Him. And it was proven in the hadith of the Night Journey narrated in the two Sahihs and others on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said in describing the Frequented House in the seventh heaven: And behold, seventy thousand angels enter it every day and they do not return to it until the last thing they are responsible for. Imam Ahmad said: Aswad told us, Isra’il told us, on the authority of Ibrahim bin Muhajir, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Mawariq, on the authority of Abu Dharr, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “I see what you do not see and I hear what you do not hear. The heavens groan, and it is right for them to groan. There is not in it the space of a finger but upon it is an angel prostrating. If you knew what I know, you would laugh little and cry much, and you would not take pleasure in women on the beds, and you would go out to the high places, beseeching God Almighty.” Abu Dharr said: By God, I would like to be a tree that is being cut down. Al-Tirmidhi and Ibn Majah narrated it from the hadith of Isra’il. Al-Tirmidhi said: It is a good, rare hadith, and it is narrated on the authority of Abu Dharr as a continuation of the hadith. Al-Hafiz Abu al-Qasim al-Tabarani said: Khair bin Arfa al-Misri told us, Urwah bin Marwan al-Raqi told us, Ubayd God bin Amr told us, on the authority of Abdul Karim bin Malik, on the authority of Ata’ bin Abi Rabah, on the authority of Jabir bin Abdullah, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: There is not in the seven heavens the space of a foot, a handspan, or a palm but that there is an angel in it. A standing angel, a prostrating angel, or a kneeling angel. Then, on the Day of Resurrection, they will all say, Glory be to You! We have not worshipped You as You should be worshipped except that we have not associated anything with You. Muhammad ibn Nasr al-Marwazi said in the Book of Prayer: Amr ibn Zararah told us, Abd al-Wahhab ibn Ata’ told us, on the authority of Sa’id, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Safwan ibn Mahraz, on the authority of Hakim ibn Hizam, who said: While the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) was with his companions, he said to them, Do you hear what I hear? They said, We do not hear anything. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said, “I hear the creaking of the sky, and you are not to be blamed for it creaking. There is not a place the size of a handspan in it except that there is an angel kneeling or prostrating on it.” He also said: Muhammad bin Abdullah bin Qahdhadh narrated to us, Abu Muadh al-Fadl bin Khalid al-Nahwi narrated to us, Ubayd bin Sulayman al-Bahili narrated to us, I heard al-Dahhak bin Muzahim narrating on the authority of Masruq bin al-Ajda’ on the authority of Aisha that she said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “There is not a place of a foot in the lowest heaven except that there is an angel prostrating or standing on it. This is the saying of the angels: ‘And there is not one of Us but has a known position. And indeed, it is We who arrange [our ranks] in rows. And indeed, it is We who glorify [God].” This is a very strange chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet. Then he narrated it on the authority of Mahmud bin Adam on the authority of Abu Mu’awiyah on the authority of al-A’mash on the authority of Abu al-Dahha on the authority of Masruq on the authority of Ibn Mas’ud that he said: There is a heaven in which there is not a place the size of a handspan except that there is an angel’s forehead or feet standing on it. Then he recited: ‘And indeed, it is We who arrange [our ranks] in rows. And indeed, it is We who glorify [God].’” Then he said: Ahmad bin Sayyar told us, Abu Ja`far bin Muhammad bin Khalid al-Dimashqi, known as Ibn Ummah, told us, al-Mughira bin `Umar bin `Atiyya from Banu `Amr bin `Awf told us, Sulayman bin Ayyub told me on the authority of Salim bin `Awf, `Ata` bin Zayd bin Mas`ud from Banu al-Hubla told me, Sulayman bin `Amr bin al-Rabi` from Banu Salim told me, `Abd al-Rahman bin al-`Ala` from Banu Sa`idah told me on the authority of his father al-`Ala` bin Sa`d, who witnessed the conquest and what came after it, that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said one day to those sitting with him: Do you hear what I hear? They said: And what do you hear, O Messenger of God? He said: “The heavens groaned, and it is right for them to groan, for there is not a place for a foot in it but that there is an angel standing, bowing, or prostrating on it. And the angels said: ‘And indeed, it is We who arrange [our ranks] and indeed, it is We who glorify.’” This is a very strange chain of transmission. Then he said: Ishaq bin Muhammad bin Ismail Al-Farawi told us, Abdul Malik bin Qudamah told us, on the authority of Abdul Rahman bin Abdullah bin Dinar, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abdullah bin Omar, “That Omar came while the prayer was being performed and three men were sitting, one of them being Abu Jahsh Al-Laithi. He said: Stand up and pray with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. Two of them stood up, but Abu Jahsh refused to stand up and said: I will not stand up until a man comes who is two arms stronger than me and has more power than me, and he wrestles me down and then thrusts my face into the dirt. Omar said: So I wrestled him down and thrust his face into the dirt. Then Uthman bin Affan came and held me back from him. Omar went out angrily until he reached the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: What do you think, O Abu Hafs? He mentioned to him what had happened, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: If Omar is pleased with him, by God, I would have liked you to bring me the head of the wicked man. Omar stood up and headed towards him, and when he was far away, he called him and said: Sit down so that I may tell you how the Lord, Blessed and Exalted be He, did not care about the prayer of Abu Jahsh, and that God, the Most High, has angels in the lowest heaven who are humble and do not raise their heads.” Their heads will be raised until the Hour comes. When it comes, they will raise their heads and say, Our Lord, we did not worship You as You should be worshipped. Indeed, in the second heaven there are angels prostrating themselves and they will not raise their heads until the Hour comes. When the Hour comes, they will raise their heads and say, Glory be to You, our Lord, we did not worship You as You should be worshipped. Umar said to him: And what do they say, O Messenger of God? He said: “As for the people of the lowest heaven, they say: ‘Glory be to the Possessor of dominion and sovereignty.’ As for the people of the second heaven, they say: ‘Glory be to the Possessor of glory and majesty.’ As for the people of the third heaven, they say: ‘Glory be to the Ever-Living who does not die.’ So say it, O Umar, in your prayer.” Umar said: O Messenger of God, what about what you taught me and commanded me to say in my prayer? He said: Say this once and this once. What he commanded him to say was: I seek refuge in your pardon from your punishment, and I seek refuge in your pleasure from your wrath, and I seek refuge in you from you, the Majestic is your face. This is a very strange hadith, in fact it is extremely strange. Al-Bukhari narrated from Ishaq al-Farawi, and Ibn Hibban mentioned him among the trustworthy ones, but Abu Dawud, al-Nasa’i, al-Uqayli, and al-Darqutni declared him weak. Abu Hatim al-Razi said: He was truthful, except that he lost his sight, so he was probably prompted, and his books are authentic. He said once: He is confused. His sheikh, Abd al-Malik ibn Qudamah, Abu Qatada al-Jumahi, also spoke against him. It is surprising that Imam Muhammad bin Nasr narrated it without speaking about it, nor knowing its condition, nor discussing the weakness of some of its men. However, he narrated it from another chain of transmission on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, with a similar mursal, and from another chain of transmission on the authority of Al-Hasan Al-Basri, with a similar mursal, close to it. Then Muhammad bin Nasr said: Muhammad bin Abdullah bin Quhadadh told us, Al-Nadr told us, Ibad bin Mansur told us: I heard Adi bin Artah, while he was delivering a sermon to us on the pulpit of Al-Madain, saying: I heard a man from the companions of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: “God Almighty has angels whose limbs tremble with fear of Him. There is not an angel among them who sheds a tear except that it falls on an angel praying. Among them are angels who have been prostrating since God created the heavens and the earth, and they have not raised their heads and will not raise them until the Day of Resurrection. Among them are angels who are bowing, and they have not raised their heads since God created the heavens and the earth and will not raise them until the Day of Resurrection. When they raise their heads, they look at the face of God, the Almighty and Majestic, and say: Glory be to You, we have not worshipped You as You should be worshipped.” This is a good chain of transmission. And the Almighty said: And it is not but a reminder to mankind. Mujahid and others said: And it is not meaning the fire that was described but a reminder to mankind. Then the Almighty said: No! By the moon * And the night when it departs meaning it turns away And the morning when it brightens meaning it shines Indeed, it is one of the greatest meaning the greatest things, meaning the fire. This was said by Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, Qatadah, Ad-Dahhak and others from the Salaf. A warner to mankind * For whoever among you wills to come forward or stay behind meaning for whoever wills to accept the warning and be guided to the truth or stay behind from it and turn away and reject it.
74:38: God Almighty says, informing us that Every soul will be held in pledge for its deeds on the Day of Resurrection, meaning it will be detained for its deeds on the Day of Resurrection. This was said by Ibn Abbas and others. Except the companions of the right hand, for they will be in gardens, questioning one another about the criminals, meaning they will question the criminals while they are in the upper rooms, and those are in the lower levels, saying to them: What has brought you into Hellfire? They will say, We were not of those who prayed, nor did we feed the poor, meaning we did not worship God nor did we treat His creation well from our kind. And we were conversing with the conversants, meaning we would talk about what we do not know. Qatada said: “Whenever a deviator went astray, we went astray with him. “And we used to deny the Day of Judgment * Until there comes to us the certainty” meaning death, as God Almighty says: And worship your Lord until there comes to you the certainty. And the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: As for him - meaning Uthman ibn Maz’un - the certainty has come to him from his Lord. God Almighty said: So what will the intercession of intercessors benefit them? That is, whoever is characterized by such qualities, the intercession of an intercessor will not benefit him on the Day of Resurrection, because intercession is only effective if the place is receptive. As for whoever meets God as a disbeliever on the Day of Resurrection, he will inevitably be in the Fire, abiding therein. Then God Almighty said: So why do they turn away from the reminder? That is, why do these disbelievers who came before you turn away from what you call them to and remind them of? As if they were wild donkeys * Fleeing from a lion that is, as if they were, in their aversion to the truth and their turning away from it, wild donkeys when they flee from a lion that wants to hunt them. This was said by Abu Hurayrah and Ibn Abbas in a narration from him and Zayd. Ibn Aslam and his son Abd al-Rahman, or Ram, which is a narration on the authority of Ibn Abbas and is the opinion of the majority. Hammad ibn Salamah said on the authority of Ali ibn Zayd on the authority of Yusuf ibn Mihran on the authority of Ibn Abbas: The lion in Arabic, and in Abyssinian it is called Qasoora, and in Persian it is Sher, and in Nabataean it is Uba. And the Almighty’s saying: Rather, every man of them desires to be given spread out pages means, rather, every one of these polytheists desires that a book be sent down to him as God sent down to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. This was said by Mujahid and others, like the Almighty’s saying: And when a sign comes to them, they say, ‘We will not believe until we are given the like of that which was given to the messengers of God.’ God knows best where to place His message. And in a narration from Qatada: They want to be given immunity without doing any deeds. So the Almighty’s saying: No! Rather, they do not fear the Hereafter means that what corrupted them was their lack of belief in it and their denial of its occurrence. Then the Almighty said: No indeed! It is a reminder. That is, truly the Qur’an is a reminder. “So whoever wills may remember it. But they will not remember except that God wills.” Like His statement: And you do not will except that God wills. And the Almighty’s statement: He is worthy of piety and of forgiveness. That is, He is worthy of being feared and He is worthy of forgiving the sin of whoever repents to Him and returns to Him. This was said by Qatada. Imam Ahmad said: Zaid bin Al-Hubab told us, Suhayl, the brother of Hazm, told me, Thabit Al-Bunani told us, on the authority of Anas bin Malik may God be pleased with him, who said: “The Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) recited this verse: ‘He is worthy of piety and forgiveness.’ He said: ‘Your Lord said: I am worthy of being feared, so let no god be associated with Me. So whoever fears that I should be associated with Me, he is worthy that I should forgive him.’” At-Tirmidhi and Ibn Majah narrated it from the hadith of Zaid bin Al-Hubab, and An-Nasa’i from the hadith of Al-Mu’afa bin Imran, both from Suhayl bin Abdullah Al-Qat’i with it. At-Tirmidhi said: It is hasan gharib, and Suhayl is not strong. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it from his father, from Hudbah bin Khalid, from Suhayl with it. Abu Ya’la, Al-Bazzar, Al-Baghawi and others narrated it in this way from the hadith of Suhayl Al-Qat’i with it. The end of the interpretation of Surat Al-Muddaththir. All praise and thanks be to God.
